hypotheses.title: Unauthenticated users can fetch /rest/admin/application-configuration
hypotheses.rationale: Endpoint is reachable by anon in the map but returns configuration that should be admin‑only
first_moves: Inspect response for sensitive config values

hypotheses.title: Unauthenticated users can fetch /rest/admin/application-version
hypotheses.rationale: Version information is exposed without login, potentially aiding exploit development

hypotheses.title: POST to /socket.io/ can be used without authentication to trigger server‑side actions
hypotheses.rationale: Endpoint is marked state_changing and allowed for anon; could be abused to manipulate server state or cause errors
first_moves: Send an empty POST to /socket.io/ as anon
Record status code and any response data

hypotheses.title: The /redirect endpoint can be abused to redirect to arbitrary external URLs
hypotheses.rationale: Page shows "Blocked" but may reflect the to‑parameter; if not validated it enables open‑redirect
first_moves: Observe whether browser follows the URL or page reflects it

hypotheses.title: Inject script payload into q parameter of /rest/products/search to achieve reflected XSS
hypotheses.rationale: Search results often echo the query term; unsanitized input may lead to script execution
first_moves: Check if the script runs in the browser

hypotheses.title: Supply huge numeric values to /api/Quantitys/ to cause integer overflow or crash
hypotheses.rationale: Endpoint likely processes numeric quantities; extreme values may break processing logic

hypotheses.title: Unauthenticated request to /api/Challenges/ reveals full challenge list including solved status
hypotheses.rationale: Challenge data is exposed to anon, leaking scoring and potentially solution hints

hypotheses.title: Rapid repeated POSTs to /socket.io/ can exhaust server resources leading to denial of service
hypotheses.rationale: No rate limiting observed for state‑changing socket endpoint; high request volume may degrade service
first_moves: Send 100 POST requests to /socket.io/ in quick succession
